title: Small-sample cluster-robust inference: CR2 with Satterthwaite df
summary: A patient-level regression in a trial with few, unequal clusters, with the Bell-McCaffrey (CR2) sandwich and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

sizing._note: A cluster trial is sized on the number of clusters; see the design-effect and simulation guidance.

pinned_defaults: R: vcov = 'CR2' and test = 'Satterthwaite'. CR0/CR1 are smaller here (CR1 1.27 vs CR2 1.33) and a z reference narrower still.

Python: no standard package implements CR2 with Satterthwaite df (statsmodels' cluster option is CR1-style with G - 1 df). Both are written out, following Bell and McCaffrey (2002) and Pustejovsky and Tipton (2018), and match clubSandwich to 1e-10, including the fractional df (8.98 here).
_when: Under about 40 clusters, and especially with unequal cluster sizes, the ordinary cluster-robust SE is too small. CR2 with Satterthwaite df keeps close to nominal coverage; the df can be far below G - 1.
